context:
Goal: Opus runs only where you granted it.
Problem (rule): on Nov 3 19:25 CST you granted "some opus judges toward the end of the workflow" on step prose-governance-workflow. A step grant can only name a role, so it was recorded as "reviewer", and today a round-3 code reviewer on that step ran Opus under it.
Based on (read): hooks/override.py takes a step grant's role as one agent role (OPUS_ROLES); it has no judge role and no brief marker.
Based on (read): the lane's guard.log, 13:19:38 CST: the step grant let an Opus spawn through on step prose-governance-workflow.
Departs from: main step grants (one role for the whole step) — adds an optional brief marker, so a grant covers only spawns whose brief starts with it.
Meanwhile: the grant record stays as it is; the step's merge does not wait on this.

lastAnswer.note: Owner: a. Routed 13:55 CST to the coordinator for the guard lane.

options.gain: The grant means what you said; other reviewers stay on Sonnet.
options.how: A step grant can require a brief whose first line is `Judge:`, like the `Audit:` marker. This grant then covers only judge spawns.
options.label: Add a Judge: marker

options.how: The lane asks you for each Opus judge with a one-act override.
options.label: Drop the grant
options.lose: One prompt to you per judge.

options.label: Keep as is
options.lose: Every reviewer on that step may run Opus.
